subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
SCOPE WIDENING IS THE OPERATIONAL CURE FOR THE FIRST-ASSIGNMENT SURPLUS COPY, AND THE DEFECT MIGRATES RATHER THAN VANISHING - SO THE CURE MUST BE APPLIED TWICE, THE SECOND TIME ONTO AN ARGUMENT SITE THAT ABSORBS IT FOR FREE. This extends claim.law.MB_ternary-result-coalesces-with-its-destination-only-after-the-first-assignment-in-scope.20260901.v1 in three ways, each measured on show_optmenu (game/ui/options.c) this run, and together they closed a two-instruction count gap that two prior records had classified as unreachable.

(1) THE MB MECHANISM IS NOT SPECIFIC TO TERNARIES. MB derived it on ternary results in mb_particle.c. Measured here on a plain three-term OR expression, `((a & 0xFF) << 16) | ((b & 0xFF) << 8) | (c & 0xFF)`, the identical shape appears: at the destination's textually FIRST assignment in its declaration scope MWCC builds the value in a scratch register and then copies it into the home, costing one surplus word, while at any LATER assignment in the same scope it builds directly into the home. Read the two failing sites against the two passing ones in the same function: the SAME expression compiled to the target's exact bytes at both sites where its result feeds an argument register directly, and paid a copy at both sites where it fed a named local at that local's first in-scope assignment. The trigger is the first-assignment position, not the operator.

(2) THE CURE THAT WORKS IS DELETING A DECLARATION, NOT RESPELLING AN EXPRESSION. MB's own prescription is 'give the destination an earlier definition in the same scope', which reads as an instruction to add a statement. The cheaper and more faithful move is to REMOVE the inner declaration entirely and reuse an existing wider-scope local of identical type that the code above has already assigned. In show_optmenu the prompt block declared `u32 rgbp;` and assigned it once; deleting that declaration and respelling its five uses to the function-scope `u32 color`, already assigned in the item loop above, removed the surplus `mr r25,r0` outright (insns 799 -> 798, multiset 4t -> 3t, fuzzy 89.1832 -> 89.8432). No expression text changed. This is also the more plausible reconstruction: the surrounding function already reuses `pc` and `idx` across sibling blocks, so a second reused accumulator is what the original author wrote.

(3) THE MIGRATION, WHICH IS THE PART THAT COSTS A LANE A BUILD IF IT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN. Widening does not delete the defect; it MOVES it to whatever is now the wider local's textually first assignment. After the edit above, the surplus copy reappeared as `addi r24,r4,0` at the item loop's `color` assignment - the new first-in-scope site. The second application is what actually closes the function, and it must target a site where the value is consumed straight into an ARGUMENT register: at such a site the coalescing is free and the first-assignment penalty is absorbed rather than paid. Giving `color` an earlier definition at the title block, where the expression had been written inline inside a DrawTextKeepScale call, cost nothing at the new site (the aligned read shows the value building directly into r6 exactly as the target does) and removed the copy at the old one. Instruction counts went 798 -> 797, EQUAL, and the ops-cluster count fell 66 -> 60.

PRACTICAL RULE. When a multi-term expression assigned to a local shows one surplus register copy: (a) locate the local's declaration scope and confirm the failing assignment is the textually first one in it; (b) look for an existing wider-scope local of the same type that is already assigned earlier, and delete the inner declaration in its favour; (c) expect the copy to reappear at the wider local's new first assignment and plan the second edit before measuring, choosing an argument-consuming site to absorb it. Do NOT probe the expression's spelling, its parenthesisation, or its term order at the failing site - MB already measured four such non-cures, and the term order is identical on both sides here.

BOUNDARY, measured, so this is not over-claimed: declaration ORDER is null for this mechanism. Two independent probes on show_optmenu - swapping `s32 savedFlags;` with `volatile s32 lh;`, and swapping `s32 hi2;` with `s32 itemfont;` - both came back NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, i.e. the object bytes did not change at all and the edit folded away before codegen. Scope WIDTH and assignment ORDER move the bytes; declaration order does not. Anyone reaching for claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1 or the block-allocation-order family to explain a surplus copy should read this boundary first: on this function those laws were screened, probed and refuted, and the measured slot-88/96 spill swap they appeared to predict is NOT declaration-order driven and remains unexplained.
